prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Mastering Your Desktop Companion Controls", "Learn the shortcuts to interact, move, or hide your companion anytime on your desktop."]
1: ["Preparing pet desktop renders and checking system screen compatibility..."]
2: ["Choose Your Ideal Desktop Companion", "Preview how your pet looks and reacts live on screen before finalizing adoption."]
3: ["Signing in backs up your pets securely so you never lose them when reinstalling or changing devices."]
4: ["Select How You Wish to Obtain Your Pet", "Pick a ready-to-adopt companion or design your custom companion from scratch."]
5: ["Official Adoption Certificate", "Name your companion and review their attributes before welcoming them home."]
6: ["Tip: Right-click the desktop pet icon in your taskbar tray anytime to hide, summon, or adjust settings."]
7: ["Generating Your Pet Renders...", "You will receive a notification as soon as your pet is ready on your desktop."]
8: ["Find Your Perfect Path", "Answer a quick preference check to get the best recommended path for your desktop setup."]
9: ["Use well-lit, clear front-facing photos for optimal 3D pet generation quality."]

verdicts.problem: requests personal photos of the user
